newsitem.title: UK: UK managers ignorant about computer threat - survey.
newsitem.headline: UK managers ignorant about computer threat - survey.

text.p: Less than a third of the senior managers in British companies are fully aware of a problem that could send their computer systems crashing when 2000 arrives, a government-sponsored survey has shown.
Technology minister Ian Taylor said on Tuesday he planned to write to 100,000 chief executives later this month to warn them of the urgent need to tackle the so-called "millennium bomb".

Industry experts have warned of possible chaos because the year in most computer programmes is expressed as a double digit -- currently 97. Unless properly reprogrammed, computers will be flummoxed by a double zero for 2000.

According to the survey, commissioned by the government's Trade and Industry Department, only nine percent of companies have so far audited their computer systems to assess how they could be affected.
"Chief executives need to wake up," Taylor said in a statement.
"Will a company which has corrected its systems be prepared to do business with one that has not made an effort to comply? I am sure that they will not." -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
